title: Listing-Duration Proration of the Failed-Sale Charge Cap (Real Estate Service Contracts)
content:
**Rule.** On a Real Estate Service Contracts listing order that ended without a closing, the failed-sale charge cap — the ceiling on the failed-sale charge billed to the seller — follows how long the listing order stayed in force. The days in force are the calendar days from the order date to the order's end date (an order whose end date is the day after its order date has been in force 1 day). The plan premium invoiced is the sum of the plan invoices on the order.

| Days in force | Failed-sale charge cap |
|---|---|
| fewer than 60 | daily proration: the plan premium invoiced times the days in force, divided by the plan's seller coverage period of 180 days, rounded to the cent |
| at least 60 but fewer than 180 | proration by months begun: the plan premium invoiced times the listing months begun, divided by 6, rounded to the cent; the listing months begun are the whole calendar months from the order date to the end date, plus one |
| 180 or more | the full plan premium invoiced |

The seller coverage period these thresholds use is the plan's own:

| Plan | Seller coverage period |
|---|---|
| Bridgewell Closing Starter, Standard, Plus, Premier and Premier Two-Year | 180 days |
| Bridgewell New Construction Three-Year | 0 days (no seller listing coverage, so no listing order) |

## Boundaries worked through (hypothetical order dated 1 March, plan premium invoiced $650.00)

| End date | Days in force | Band | Cap |
|---|---|---|---|
| 15 April | 45 | fewer than 60 | $650.00 times 45 divided by 180: $162.50 |
| 29 April | 59 | fewer than 60 | $650.00 times 59 divided by 180: $213.06 |
| 30 April | 60 | 60 to 179 | 1 whole month plus one gives 2 months begun; $650.00 times 2 divided by 6: $216.67 |
| 27 August | 179 | 60 to 179 | 5 whole months plus one gives 6 months begun; $650.00 times 6 divided by 6: $650.00 |
| 28 August | 180 | 180 or more | the full $650.00 |

## Basis Q&A

**Which end date is used?** The order's end date as recorded when the listing order expired or was cancelled.

**Is a part month counted under the months-begun method?** Yes: the whole calendar months from the order date to the end date are counted and one more month is added for the month begun.
